Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed collision in a parking lot with complaints of neck and low back pain and muscle
stiffness. The reported mechanism of injury is consistent with the findings documented at intake. Over the course of 22 visits,
care consisted of manual therapy, targeted therapeutic exercise, and home exercise instruction, progressing in a typical manner
for soft tissue strain. Range of motion and strength improved steadily, and visit frequency was gradually reduced as symptoms
resolved. Imaging and physical examination findings clearly confirm the presence of cervical and lumbar strain. No prior
complaints or treatment involving these body regions are known from the patient history reviewed. Billed services align with the
documented plan of care, with no repeated or duplicate charges identified. Patient was discharged to self-directed home exercise
with instructions to return if symptoms recur.

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.

- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
